name: WWFL World Heavyweight Belt
epitaph: Named first among six belts in the fed's own complete rulebook (1 Dec 1997); two reigns are now on record from the fed's own 1998 broadcasts, with a further title change referenced but not yet confirmed to a servable standard.

name: WWFL Intercontinental Belt
epitaph: Changed hands twice around the fed's own December 1997 pay-per-view before settling into one of the promotion's longest-held reigns, its holder's own broadcasts calling it the longest in WWFL history.

name: WWFL United States Belt
epitaph: Named in the fed's own complete rulebook; no roster, card, or champion survives in this collection's holdings.

name: WWFL Cage Belt
epitaph: Winnable only inside a steel cage; stripped from a holder by the fed's own president in February 1998 and won back through a tournament before changing hands again in a post-match ambush at the fed's own annual flagship event.

name: WWFL Cruiserweight Belt
epitaph: The fed's own light-weight belt, held by a future WWFL headliner before passing through a fire-breathing champion on its way to one of the promotion's own rising stars.

name: WWFL Tag Team Titles
epitaph: The fed's own only tag championship, changing hands once in the collection's own held record on the strength of a returning team's own comeback win.

name: WWFL Television Championship
epitaph: A belt the fed introduced into its own 1998 record after its original six; held by its own reigning wrestler through the last held WWFL broadcast.
